messages:
alyssa: hey team — real quick: i'm mid-travel and just got a page from prod-monitoring for eu-1. i'm nominally primary for tonight but i need to step away for ~3h to sort an urgent thing IRL. can someone take primary until ~02:15 UTC? i've left notes and the runbook link below.

oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Paging alert (severity: high) — 5xx spike on /v1/generate in eu-1. Current alert count: 47 in the last 5m. Incident created: INC-2026-045.

kevin: I can grab primary for the next 3 hours. leaving my calendar blocked. can you DM me any sticky state or ongoing mitigations?

alyssa: thanks kevin — quick state: customers seeing elevated latency + 5xx. traffic surge to a subset of model workers (shard 12-14). autoscaler didn't kick because request pattern is bursty short-lived. mitigation in flight was to redirect eu traffic to eu-fallback pool (lower-capacity) and enable prefix-cache bypass for the longest prompts.

samira: i'll be secondary shadowing. going to open the runbook and check current KV cache hit rates. link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/eu-5xx-spike

micha: FYI ops-bot already applied a conservative routing rule to steer 20% to dedicated-dyno-2 as a circuit-breaker. see ops-bot event below.

ops-bot: Applied temporaryRoutingRule(id=tr-992) — steer 20% of eu-1 traffic to dedicated-dyno-2. Reason: reduce burst pressure on shard12-14. Rollback window: 30m. Triggered by: INC-2026-045.

kevin: acked. i'm taking primary. first actions: (1) confirm whether dedicated-dyno-2 is saturated, (2) check worker logs on shards 12-14 for OOMs or kernel errors, (3) flush stale KV prefixes for the longest prompt hash bucket.

samira: i'll jump on logs and runbook step 3. quick snippet to check KV hit rate: 
```bash
curl -s "https://metrics.internal/api/kv/hits?shard=12" | jq '.rate'
```

alyssa: pinned note: if we need to scale, use the below autoscaler command — but watch GPU mem usage:
```bash
redwoodctl autoscale set --pool eu-1 --min 8 --max 24 --policy conservative
```

micha: logs show elevated `cuda_memory_error` on worker-12 around 01:08 UTC, repeated 4x. attaching snippet of the tail: 
```
[01:08:12] worker-12 kernel: cuda: allocation failed: out of memory size=1.5G
[01:08:12] worker-12 inference: retrying chunk, kvcache flush recommended
```

kevin: ok that points to memory pressure + bursty large prompts. immediate step: keep routing rule, set prefix cache bypass for longest prompts (which reduced mean token path earlier), and spin up 2 warm workers in eu-fallback pool. I'll run the spinup and post PID.

kevin: running spin-up now — `redwoodctl worker start --pool eu-fallback --count 2 --config low-latency` (ETA ~2m).

samira: while spin-up happens i'll run a quick customer impact check: which customers are seeing errors? `prod-query` returned top 3 tenants: tenant-phi, tenant-zetta, tenant-infra. tenant-phi accounts for ~55% of the spike.

alyssa: important: tenant-phi has an active job that sends very long prompts. recommend we reach out via support channel if we expect >30m disruption.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-045 updated: mitigation in progress — routing rule active, 2 fallback workers starting. Severity remains high.

kevin: fallback workers up (IDs: wf-772, wf-773). initial health checks green. metrics show 18% drop in 5xx on eu overall. i'll monitor for 10m then decide if autoscale bump needed.

samira: confirming KV hit ratio improved from 12% -> 46% after prefix bypass. errors per min down from 9 -> 3.

alyssa: thanks all. i'm still stepping away but will be reachable by DM if anything chaotic. kevin — want me to hand over the primary badge in the rota?

kevin: yes please transfer primary to me in the oncall rota. i'll update status page if we need extended maintenance.

alyssa: done — rota shows kevin as primary until 02:15 UTC. samira as secondary. i've added a short note in the runbook with steps we took and who to contact for tenant-phi.

samira: i'll prep a short postmortem note draft in #inc-postmortems once we stabilize.

kevin: all good — monitoring looks stable for now. i'll keep primary until 02:15 UTC and then hand back to alyssa if she's available. thanks for quick take. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-045 — monitoring indicates decreased error rate. Keeping incident open for observation window (30m).

kevin: closing loop: customer-impact: tenant-phi saw ~12% failed requests during the spike window; no data loss, transient errors only. recommended follow-ups: (1) reach out to tenant-phi support, (2) evaluate autoscaler sensitivity to bursty short-lived traffic, (3) consider proactive warmup for large prompt workloads.

samira: noted. drafting follow-ups now.

alyssa: thanks everyone — appreciate the handoff. back to travel mode.
